Subject: Shared vs Private SLA rubric & next steps

Hi Aditi —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the three deployment paths we discussed (high level) so you can share with the CarePath team:

- Hosted API (Redwood-hosted): fastest to production, automatic scaling, transparent per-token billing. Tradeoffs: shared infra means potential noisy-neighbor risk; we provide SLOs and soft isolation plus per-customer throttling.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool): predictable throughput and stronger isolation guarantees (dedicated hosts / pools). Good for predictable heavy workloads and improved noisy-neighbor protection.
- Private VPC / on-prem: full network isolation, VPC peering or air-gapped options, customer-managed network and KMS. Best for regulatory/PHI scenarios but longer procurement/onboarding.

Your requirements I recorded on the call: P95 inference latency target ~120ms for shorter prompts, peak throughput ~250 tps (bursty), sustained ~50 tps, US data residency, and SOC 2 evidence during procurement. You also flagged procurement preference for a license model (rather than transient infra) if we go private.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll draft a short SLA/rubric that maps CarePath requirements to a recommended deployment path and isolation mitigations (this doc will include SLO thresholds, fallback policies, and a minimal instrumentation checklist).
2) Technical team (Ben) to outline noisy-neighbor mitigations and expected cost delta between hosted vs dedicated.
3) Marissa to prepare procurement starter pack (pricing ranges, contract cadence, procurement timeline).
4) CarePath: confirm peak pattern (are the 250 tps spikes typically <30s or multi-minute?) and the list of security controls you need included in the contract.

Attached: a short workbook I’ll iterate on (redwood-deploy-options.xlsx) — will add the SLA rubric in the next note.

If that plan works, can we target a follow-up next week (Wed/Thu) to review the rubric and decide whether a short POC on Dedicated is warranted?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Throughput: the 250 tps spikes are generally tied to end-of-day batch jobs and short windows (most spikes are under 2 minutes, but we do occasionally see 5–10 minute surges during reporting). Sustained 50 tps is correct for daytime usage.
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II is required for procurement sign-off, and we need a written statement on data residency (US-only) and retention controls.
- Procurement: yes, if Private is chosen we will prefer a fixed-term license model; otherwise for Dedicated we’d expect a reserved capacity contract.

Can you also include a very rough cost ballpark between hosted/dedicated/private (order-of-magnitude is fine for now) so I can set expectations with Procurement. I’ve attached our internal requirements sheet (carepath_requirements.xlsx) for reference.

Happy to meet next Wed (5/5) after 11am PT.

Best,

Aditi — thanks, got the requirements workbook. I pulled together an initial rubric and a short mapping of your asks to our recommended guardrails (attached: redwood-deploy-options.xlsx). High level: 

- Recommendation: run a short Dedicated POC first. Rationale: meets isolation/SLO targets without the procurement delay of Private; gives you predictable throughput and stronger noisy-neighbor protection. If procurement needs a Private/VPC license later, we can plan a migration path.

- SLA / SLO suggestions (initial):
  * P95 latency target: 120ms (short prompts), P99 < 350ms (with fallback variant).
  * Availability: 99.9% regionally for Dedicated (we can discuss higher SLAs for Private).
  * Graceful degradation: automatic fallback to a lower-cost model variant + priority queueing for critical routes.

- Isolation mitigations to include in the rubric: dedicated GPU pools per customer, prefix/KV cache partitioning, request-level throttles and quotas, and per-tenant telemetry (latency/cost traces).

Action items for our team (internal):
- Ben: prepare technical appendix on noisy-neighbor mitigations and expected performance delta (Jordan: can you prioritize this for Monday?).
- Marissa: draft procurement summary with ballpark ARR ranges for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.

Aditi — I’ll add concrete numbers in the workbook and bring the rubric to the 5/5 follow-up.

Thanks,
Jordan

Quick technical note and proposed mitigation plan for noisy-neighbor / isolation sections of the rubric. Summary first, then recommended items we should include in the SLA appendix: 

Summary: Dedicated capacity with per-customer GPU pools + strict KV/prefix cache partitioning covers ~85–90% of noisy-neighbor scenarios for inference workloads like CarePath. For residual risk we propose a three-tier fallback and instrumentation approach.

Recommended appendix items (to include verbatim in the rubric):
- Isolation: dedicated GPU pools (hard isolation at the host level) for Dedicated deployments; for Hosted we offer soft isolation via scheduling priorities and per-tenant cgroup limits.
- Cache & KV: logical partitioning of KV cache per tenant, with eviction policies tuned to your longer prompt sizes.
- Fallbacks (ordered): 1) micro-burst throttling + user-facing retry guidance; 2) automatic model variant fallback (smaller quantized variant) for non-critical routes; 3) route-based prioritization & circuit-breaker for maintenance windows.
- Observability: per-tenant token-level latency and cost traces, histograms (P50/P95/P99), and automated regression alerts tied to your canonical prompt set.
- SLOs we recommend capturing: P95 latency 120ms, P99 350ms, 99.9% availability for Dedicated. Also include an error budget policy and escalation points (who to notify and recommended remediation steps).

Estimated cost delta (very rough order-of-magnitude):
- Hosted: baseline (pay-as-you-go) — lowest up-front but higher long-run per-token cost.
- Dedicated: ~2.5–3x hosted baseline for committed capacity (lower per-token at steady-state, predictable).
- Private: variable; includes one-time on-prem/onboarding and license/ops cost — typically highest TCO but best for compliance.

I attached the internal playbook we use for isolation POCs (isolation-playbook.pdf). Action items: I will draft the appendix today and Jordan can merge into the rubric sheet; Marissa — can you slot the procurement summary and ballpark pricing into the shared workbook so we have a single source for the 5/5 meeting?
